apps.name: AirCard-iOS
apps.subtitle: Apple Wallet card skins, passcode themes and wallpapers
apps.localizedDescription: Customize Apple Wallet card artwork, lock screen passcode dialers and PosterBoard wallpapers directly on device, without a jailbreak. Requires iOS 27 or newer, LocalDevVPN running in loopback mode, and Developer Mode pairing.

versions.localizedDescription:
## What's Changed in v1.3.2 🚀

This update brings full feature parity with AirCard macOS v1.2.6, restores robust card discovery across all iOS versions, introduces automatic bank/network recognition with custom card nicknames, delivers an ultra-fast tunnel cache (0.02s connections), and completely resolves wallpaper flashing for Collections and Mercury wallpapers.

### 💳 Wallet Card Discovery & Bank Identification
• **Universal Wallet Log Parser**: Ported the proven `WalletScanParser` from AirCard macOS. Captures cards from `Dashboard loading (...): for SOO+`, `passIDs[InSession]`, `passIDs[global]`, and modern JSON NFC activations (`"identifier": "HEX"`).
• **Automatic Bank & Network Detection**: Recognizes Visa, Mastercard, American Express, UnionPay, Discover, and JCB via applet AIDs during selection.
• **Card Nicknames (Rename)**: Added a direct **Rename** button (✏️) so you can give your cards friendly names like *"Monobank"*, *"Salary Card"*, or *"Revolut"*, safely persisted in app settings.
• **28-Character Fallback Token Matcher**: Restores dependable card discovery on devices where standard log patterns are redacted.

### ⚡ Ultra-Fast Tunnel Routing (from 10s to 0.02s!)
• **Working Route Caching**: `rust-core` now caches the active RSD connection route (`LAST_WORKING_ROUTE`), eliminating repeated port and interface scanning.
• **RSD-First Priority**: Connects directly via RemoteXPC on port 49152, bypassing slow Lockdown retries and broken pipes on iOS 18+.
• **Eliminated Loopback Policy Drops**: Removed local loopback attempts that caused `policy drop` control channel errors.

### 🖼 Wallpapers (.tendies) — Collections & Mercury Fixes
• **Dual Injection on iOS 18+**: Wallpapers are now injected into both their primary bundle (`com.apple.WallpaperKit.CollectionsPoster` or `com.apple.MercuryPoster`) and the modern iOS 18+ application container (`com.apple.Posters.CollectionsPosterApp` / `com.apple.Posters.MercuryPosterApp`).
• **Metadata Synchronization**: Fixed a critical issue where `Wallpaper.plist`'s numeric identifier was randomized out-of-sync with `suggestionMetadata.plist` (`7400.DYNAMIC`), causing wallpapers like Windows 11 to vanish from the Lock Screen gallery.
• **Mercury Wallpaper Support**: Added recognition for `mercury-descriptors` container folders and registered `com.apple.Posters.MercuryPosterApp` in `PersistedPosterContainerBundleIdentifiers`.
• **NeoSpring Respring**: Instant springboard reload to apply wallpaper preferences immediately.

### 🧪 Quality & Testing
• All 24 unit tests passing (`TendiesEngineTests`, `WalletScanParserTests`, `CardPhotoCropTests`, `CardPhotoPickerTests`).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Mak5er/AirCard-iOS/compare/v1.3.1...v1.3.2

apps.name: AniBaka
apps.subtitle: 跨平台番剧聚合、媒体播放与弹幕客户端
apps.localizedDescription: AniBaka 是一个基于 Flutter 的跨平台番剧聚合与媒体播放客户端，支持多番剧源、弹幕、字幕、离线缓存与本地媒体库，并提供动漫实时超分辨率画质增强。

versions.localizedDescription:
本次更新重点优化手机端打开番剧详情和返回的体验，新增本地字体导入，并更新四个内置播放源。

### 界面与交互

- **优化番剧详情转场。** 点击卡片后，圆角小窗口从封面位置逐渐铺满全屏，返回时收回卡片。适配 Android 预测性返回和 iOS 侧滑返回手势。
- **支持导入自定义字体。** 在「设置 → 外观 → 导入字体」选择本地 `.ttf` 或 `.otf` 文件，重启应用后会恢复已导入的字体。
- **调整移动端底部导航。** 优化拖动切换和随滚动收起、显示的交互。社区发帖按钮随底栏一同收起。

### 性能优化/修复

- 优化 Android 首页触摸采样和海报网格绘制，减轻慢速滚动时的细节抖动。
- 减少封面加载、详情刷新和播放选源时的重复处理。内存紧张时释放部分后台标签页。
- 修复ios和macos异常播放器黑屏的问题。

### 播放

- 修复部分 HLS 视频因上游返回重复响应头而无法正常读取分片的问题。

### 平台兼容

- 统一 Android 各架构安装包的版本号，避免同一版本因架构不同而被识别为不同构建。
- 同步 iOS 和 macOS 的媒体库与播放器渲染插件版本，并更新 Windows 打包流程以兼容六位构建号。
**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/AniBakaBaka/AniBaka/compare/5.2.4+1101...5.2.5+261113

apps.name: Apollo for Reddit - GLASS
apps.subtitle: Apollo-Reborn build with Liquid Glass patch
apps.localizedDescription:
Apollo-Reborn is the community-maintained Apollo sideload build powered by the Apollo-Reborn tweak.

It restores custom API support, media fixes, uploads, inline media, translation, saved categories, Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets, Liquid Glass support on iOS 26+, and the rest of the project’s ongoing fixes and enhancements.

These sources are intended for AltStore Classic, SideStore, and Feather. Apollo-Reborn is not compatible with AltStore PAL.

Choose the source variant that matches how you sideload:

• Standard: full app bundle with Apollo’s working extensions plus Apollo-Reborn widgets
• No Extensions: strips app extensions, including widgets, to reduce App ID usage on free Apple IDs
• GLASS: adds the Liquid Glass iOS 26 patch and bundled Liquid Glass icon catalog
• No Extensions + GLASS: combines both options

The extension-bearing builds (Standard and GLASS) register about 7 App IDs, one per bundled app extension. A free Apple ID can register 10 App IDs per 7 days, so a clean single install fits, but it is easy to exceed if you install under more than one bundle ID, reinstall within the same week, or sideload other extension-bearing apps. If an install fails with an App ID error, use a No Extensions build (1 App ID) or wait for older App IDs to expire. A paid Apple Developer account has a much higher cap.

This project is not affiliated with Apollo or Christian Selig.

versions.localizedDescription:
### Features

- Add a **Subreddit Switcher** choice of **Classic** or **Modern** under Interface → Display & Navigation: Classic brings back Apollo's original Favorites popup for title taps and Posts tab holds, and Modern keeps the search sheet (#1604: @IllIIllIllIllII)
  - Classic is the default on regular iPhones, so updating from 4.0.x brings the popup back; Modern is the default on iPhone Duo
  - Modern now opens with the keyboard up and starts loading your pick right away, and on the iPhone Duo holding the Posts tab opens the switcher from the side rail and when unfolded
- Add **Jump Button Navigation** so the comment jump button can step through comments posted since your last visit instead of top-level threads; press and hold to go back one (#1506: @IllIIllIllIllII)
  - Choose Threads (default) or New Comments under Settings → General below Jump Button Position, or from a post's ••• menu; the button shows a NEW label in that mode
- Add **Tint Tab Bar Icons** to give unselected tab icons a muted shade of your theme's accent, on the classic and Liquid Glass tab bars and the iPhone Duo side rail (#1684: @IllIIllIllIllII, @AcornElf)
  - Add **Accent Navigation Buttons** on Liquid Glass to draw Back, toolbar and menu buttons in your theme's accent; titles stay neutral
  - Both are off by default under Settings → Appearance → Theme Manager → Options
- Add **Unread Badges** under Interface to show the Inbox's unread count as a small dot on the tab bar and on the Inbox's Notifications and Chat tabs, and to color unread badges with your theme's accent instead of red (#1680: @icpryde, @AcornElf)
  - Compact Dot on Tab Bar, Compact Dot in Inbox (shown while modern Chat is on) and Theme Color are each off by default
- Show **Hidden & Deleted** in Apollo's own post and comment lists, so results follow your post size, thumbnails, text size, themes, swipe actions and menus, and open their threads like anywhere else (#1485: @IllIIllIllIllII)
  - Items keep their Hidden, Removed or Deleted label, removed posts keep their saved title and media, and the Posts tab has its own Compact Posts / Large Thumbnails button

apps.name: ARMSX2
apps.subtitle: PlayStation 2 emulator for ARM64
apps.localizedDescription: A free and open-source PlayStation 2 (PS2) emulator based on PCSX2, with native ARM64 JIT recompilers. Play PS2 games on your phone, PC, or gaming handheld.

versions.localizedDescription:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64.AppImage, for 4K, 16K and 64K page kernels alike
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.
- iOS: your old nightly is the ARMSX2 iOS app and still has your saves. Copy them into ARMSX2 Nightly with the Files app.

## What's new
- EE: charge taking an exception 9 cycles, as the console takes
- EE: charge ERET 6 cycles, as the console takes
- EE rec: do not charge a cycle the interpreter does not after ERET, SYSCALL and EI
- EE: charge SYNC.P 5 cycles, as the console takes
- microVU: keep the program cache in a few large blocks, bounded by the RAM cap
- iOS: put EmulatorBridge on the main actor
- iOS: put ExternalGameLibrary on the main actor
- iOS: type NumberRowActivity's closure for the main actor
- iOS: drop @unchecked Sendable from the controller image cache
- iOS: put PadLayoutStore on the main actor
- iOS: put the pad preset and skin library stores on the main actor
- iOS: enable cheats through SettingsStore
- iOS: read the boot and logging keys through SettingsStore
- iOS: make the dynamic thumbstick settings a SettingsStore sub-store
- iOS: read the RetroAchievements keys through SettingsStore
- iOS: push the haptics setting to the rumble path
- iOS: keep the DEV9 hosts in SettingsStore.Network
- iOS: drop the duplicate upscale write in dynamic resolution
- iOS: test that shared names are declared once
- iOS: declare the menu sound names once
- iOS: type the game library dictionary keys
- iOS: type the RetroAchievements state keys
- iOS: type the per-game settings dictionary keys
- iOS: declare the shared notification names once
- EE: charge MOVZ and MOVN 1 cycle
- EE: charge stores 1 cycle, as the console takes
- EE: charge loads 1 cycle, as the console takes
- EE: charge MFHI, MFLO, MTHI, MTLO and the SA moves 1 cycle, as the console takes
- EE: charge the integer ALU ops, shifts, LUI, SLT and NOP 1 cycle, as the console takes
- EE: charge NOP its table entry in the recompiler
- libretro CI: drop the Android page size argument
- Android: build and ship one core library, libemucore.so
- Android: read the host page size at load time
- Android: describe what applyPadButton does with p_range
- Android: drop unchanged USB pad reports on the reader thread
- Android: rumble for a DualShock 3 under the USB takeover
- Android: keep a DualShock 3 button pressed while its pressure reads 0
- Android: native DualShock 3 button pressure over USB
- Linux arm64: pad shared structures to 128 bytes, warn only on a smaller line
- tests: drop host_page_test, its tests already run in common_test and recompiler_tests
- Linux arm64: detect host page geometry at runtime
- iOS: stop SettingsStore's init from starting GameSession
- iOS: move the DEV9 settings into SettingsStore.Network
- iOS: move the controller settings into SettingsStore.Controller
- iOS: move the appearance preferences into SettingsStore.Appearance
- iOS: make the setting descriptors static tables in their domain files
- iOS: move the types and ranges out of SettingsStore.swift
- iOS: stop three background flags rewriting themselves at launch

Full changelog: https://github.com/ARMSX2/ARMSX2/compare/nightly-20261122...d8d9a02783bef9521db7f0e62aaa6e9aebeb72f8

apps.name: Asspp
apps.subtitle: The ultimate multi-region App Store manager
apps.localizedDescription:
Manage multiple Apple IDs across App Store regions: switch stores instantly, browse and download official IPAs from anywhere, and keep a searchable IPA library with older versions — no signing out of your device required.

Downloads go through Apple's servers with your own Apple ID. Because the underlying protocol is the same one ipatool uses, a secondary or burner account is strongly recommended.

versions.localizedDescription:
## Changes

- Recover downloads when Apple returns an empty HTTP 500 by retrying the version-pinned request through the bag’s update endpoint.
- Update ApplePackage to 2.0.3 with Swift 6.2 compatibility fixes.
- Report Keychain save failures before completing login, and preserve stored data when loading fails.
- Improve empty account layout, editable device identifiers, and account table column widths.
- Remove personal metadata from bundled installation certificates and omit the CA private key.
- Explicitly clear development teams for release builds and check packaged artifacts before publication.

## Installation certificate

The local installation CA was replaced to remove personal metadata. If you use OTA installation, install and trust the new certificate from Settings after updating.

The release contains an unsigned iOS IPA and a macOS ZIP without a personal development team.

apps.name: BCD
apps.subtitle: Windows games on iPhone and iPad
apps.localizedDescription: A fast, controller-friendly launcher that runs Windows games on iOS and iPadOS with Steam and GOG built in, powered by Wine, FEX and Metal via DXMT.

versions.localizedDescription:
**BCD is in alpha:** an early stage of development, before beta. Many games run, many do not yet, and things can break between builds. When a game fails, please send a log.

> **Everything new in this release is experimental and has been tried on only a few devices so far.** It may work great on yours, or it may not work at all. Either way, a log helps a lot.

> **Tried a game on an earlier build? Reset its settings first.** On the game's page: **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**. The recommended list changed for 78 games in this release.

This build brings everything since 0.1.686: X-Plane 12 getting further, frame generation and an FPS counter for Vulkan games, Valve's November 2026 Steam client for BCD Dock, an experimental Steam for Windows, new pages in Settings, a round of fixes from the logs you sent, and a fix for Epic games on an external drive.

## X-Plane 12 (experimental)

X-Plane 12 gets further than before. On one iPhone it loaded, drew its cockpit and flew for six minutes. It is slow, it has been tried on that one iPhone only, and it is still experimental.

- **What you need:** iOS 26 or later and a device with a Metal 4 GPU. Start the game from your Steam library through BCD Dock, the way it was tried. On the game's page choose **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**. The recommended settings carry everything below.
- **Lowest graphics settings (new):** the recommended settings now carry `xplane-graphics = lowest`.
  - **Why:** X-Plane saves its preferences only when it quits cleanly, and it never had. So every start took X-Plane's default settings and went straight into its first-time flight, with no main menu to lower them in. At those defaults the game stopped twice with "X-Plane is totally out of memory" and "Failed to allocate a GPU buffer", each time with BCD's address space full.
  - **What it does:** before X-Plane starts, BCD sets the default of each of its 14 graphics settings, in X-Plane's own `Resources/settings.txt`, to the lowest value. X-Plane's safe mode and every other byte of the file stay as they were. What you save in X-Plane still wins over these defaults.
  - **Going back:** X-Plane's own file is kept as `settings.txt.bcd-original` and put back when the line is removed.
- **A 4 GB swap file (new):** the recommended settings now carry `swap-mb = 4096`, `swap-mode = 2` and `swap-min-mb = 1`. BCD then moves game data to a file on the device's storage when memory runs short. Without it iOS ended the app at its 8 GB limit while the flight loaded (5 GB at the menu, 8.1 GB three minutes later). With it the flight ran for six minutes at a peak of 6.8 GB, and X-Plane quit cleanly from its own menu.
- **A freeze while loading:** one log showed the game compiling about 700 shader libraries over eight minutes. Then one more compile, a Metal library with no shader source, was still running 96 seconds later, and the game never drew again. BCD now refuses such a request at once instead of sending it to Metal's compiler. This was checked on a Mac. On the iPhone the next run took every shader from the cache, so the refusal itself has not been seen working there yet.
- **FPS counter:** it never worked for X-Plane, because Vulkan games did not reach it. It does now (see below).
- **What to expect:** about 13 to 18 FPS in flight at the lowest settings. The first start compiles shaders for several minutes (about 700 compiles over eight minutes in one log); later starts read them from the cache.
- **With frame generation** (below) X-Plane reached about 35 FPS shown in flight on that iPhone, from about 15 of its own (the HUD's `15+15`). iPads and other iPhones have not been tried. If it fails on yours, please send a log.

## Frame generation and the FPS counter for Vulkan games (experimental)

Vulkan games now get a working FPS counter and the frame-rate limit, on MoltenVK and on KosmicKrisp. Vulkan games that run on KosmicKrisp (the game's **Vulkan (experimental)** choice set to **KosmicKrisp**, which needs iOS 26 and a Metal 4 GPU) also get frame generation. X-Plane 12 on one iPhone is the only game and device all of this has run on so far: with frame generation it showed about 35 FPS in flight.

- **Apple frame interpolation:** on the game's page, **Display › Apple frame interpolation**: one frame between two, or up to three. iOS's own video frame interpolation makes the extra pictures from two of the game's frames. It needs no help from the game. It needs iOS 26, and it works only on KosmicKrisp, not on MoltenVK.
- **Lossless Scaling frame generation:** on the game's page, **Display › Lossless Scaling frame generation**: 2×, 3× or 4×.
  - **Lossless Scaling is not part of BCD.** It is a program sold on Steam. You need your own copy: sign in to Steam in BCD, then **Settings › Graphics › Lossless Scaling › Check my purchase and download from Steam**, once. BCD asks Steam whether your account owns it, downloads it with your account, and keeps its file sealed on this device. The purchase is checked again every week.
  - **For a Vulkan game,** BCD translates Lossless Scaling's frame generation shaders to Metal on the device when the game starts, from your own copy. The passes are then built in the background, which takes about 2 to 3 seconds. The translated file is removed when the session ends.
  - With Lossless Scaling on, Apple frame interpolation stays off for that game: one generator at a time.
- **Generated frames add a little delay.** They help most when the GPU has room to spare.
- **The frame-rate limit now holds Vulkan games,** on MoltenVK and on KosmicKrisp, as it always held DirectX games. Before, a Vulkan game ran at the screen's own rate whatever the limit said: X-Plane's menu ran at 120 FPS with the limit at 60. **This changes every Vulkan game:** one that ran above its limit now runs at it. `env.MADEIRA_VK_FPS_CAP = 0` in a game's settings turns it off. For Vulkan games the limit holds the game's own frames, and the generated frames come on top.
- **The FPS counter and the session summary now cover Vulkan games.** Before, every Vulkan game showed 0 FPS.
- **The in-game HUD shows the frames frame generation made,** after the game's own rate: `15+15 FPS` is 15 frames of the game's and 15 that frame generation made.
  - It counts Apple frame interpolation, Lossless Scaling and MetalFX frame generation, in DirectX games (through DXMT and BCD's Direct3D 12 bridge) and in Vulkan games on KosmicKrisp.
  - The frame time, the lows and the graph stay the game's own. The colour judges every frame shown against the limit.
  - Before, Lossless Scaling's frames in a Direct3D 11 game were counted as the game's own, so the rate was the sum of both.
  - On a device, this was seen only in X-Plane 12 (Vulkan). The DirectX paths were checked by tests, not yet on a device.
- **Not done:** Apple frame interpolation for Vulkan games on MoltenVK.

## The November 2026 Steam client in BCD Dock, and why you don't need Steam for Windows to play (experimental)

### What BCD Dock is
- BCD Dock starts your Steam games through **Valve's own Steam client library** (`steamclient64.dll`, the file the full Steam app for Windows also uses). It runs inside BCD without Steam's window, its web browser (Chromium) and its library.
- BCD Dock signs in with your own Steam sign-in. Valve's client then does what a game needs from Steam, as it does on a PC:
  - the online sign-in and the check that you own the game;
  - the game's Steam calls and any Steam DRM the game carries;
  - the per-account programs some games need (BCD Dock asks the client to prepare them before the start);
  - signing in offline;
  - Friends in games, when you turn them on in **Settings › Accounts › Steam**.
- BCD Dock is not a Steam emulator and bypasses nothing. Without Valve's sign-in and licence answer, a game does not start.

### What the November 2026 client adds
- **Settings › BCD Dock › Steam client** now offers three builds of Valve's client:
  - **Jan 2026**, the default, unchanged;
  - **Sep 2026**, unchanged: for games that ask for a newer Steam interface than January's has, such as Grim Dawn, Hades II and Enshrouded. No Friends;
  - **Nov 2026**, new: the client Valve published on 13 November 2026.
- **Newer Steam interfaces.** Nov 2026 has five interfaces that the January client lacks: `SteamUser024`, `SteamInput007`, `SteamNetworkingSockets013`, `SteamGameServer016` and `SteamMatchMakingServers003`. A game built with a newer Steam library can stop at its start with "Missing interface adapter", with "No SteamUtils011" or with a "Steam is not running" box. Nov 2026 has the newer interfaces such a game asks for. A game may still ask for something newer than Valve's client of 13 November has.
- **Friends** work with Nov 2026, as with Jan 2026. Sep 2026 has none.
- **BCD's suggestions** now name Nov 2026 when a game stops because its Steam library is newer than the client (for `SteamUtils011`, Sep 2026 has the interface too).
- **Switching** moves your installed games, saves and settings to the chosen client, and you can switch back at any time. The old client's folder is renamed and kept. Nothing is deleted.
- **A build BCD Dock does not know is refused before sign-in** with report code 30, not guessed at. BCD Dock checks the exact client file and the exact calls it makes into it, build by build. Valve moved four of the client's internal calls (the two ownership questions and the two offline sign-in calls) by one slot in this build, so each build now has its own table.
- **Tried so far,** on one iPhone: the switch to Nov 2026 and back; games started through BCD Dock; a game whose per-account program Steam prepares; an offline start; Friends; a game that stopped on a missing Steam interface. The table for this build was made by reading Valve's file, without a device. These runs are its first tests.
- **January 2026 stays the default.** Nov 2026 is less tested. Choose it when a game needs it. If a game no longer starts with it, switch back.

### Why you don't need Steam for Windows to play
- **The game already talks to Valve's real client.** Sign-in, ownership, Steam's calls, per-account programs, offline play and Friends all go through the same client library that BCD Dock runs. The full Steam app adds a window around that library. A game does not need the window.
- **Memory.** Steam's window is a web browser. On the one iPhone tried it held 2.3 to 3.4 GB of the 8 GB iOS gives BCD, much of BCD's address space and a JIT pool of up to 1.1 GB for its own code. Heavy games need all of that for themselves. Through BCD Dock they get it.
- **Each game's own BCD settings.** Through BCD Dock every game starts with its recommended settings and the ones you set on its page. A game started from Steam for Windows runs inside Steam's session, with that session's settings. X-Plane 12, started that way, found no Vulkan driver and quit after nine seconds.
- **BCD's own library covers the rest:** downloads and updates, DLC you own, beta versions, Workshop items, Steam Cloud saves and Launch options.

### When Steam for Windows can still help
These are things BCD itself does not do:
- buying games or DLC in the Steam store;
- Steam's own settings and account pages, and Steam's community pages;
- your friends list and chat outside a game (BCD offers Friends in a game);
- your achievements: BCD does not show them;
- updating a game that Valve's client installed in its own library folder. BCD lists and starts such a game but does not update it.

Steam's app on your phone, or Steam's website, can do most of these too.

## Steam for Windows (experimental, off unless you turn it on): not for playing games

> **Steam for Windows is not a way to play your games.** Play them through BCD Dock, as before. Turn this on only if you want to look around in Valve's own Steam app.

- **What it is:** Valve's full Steam client for Windows, with its own window, store and library, in a Windows desktop inside BCD. Turn it on in **Settings › BCD Dock › Steam for Windows**, then install it there. BCD gets it from Valve's own servers and checks every file. You sign in in Steam's own window; BCD hands it no sign-in.
- **What it is for:** the store, your library, Friends, the Workshop and Steam's own settings.
- **Why not for games:** a game started from it runs inside Steam's own session. It does not get the settings BCD gives that game, and Steam's window uses much of the memory a game needs. Heavy games do not fit beside it. In tests on one iPhone it opened, signed in and showed the library, but the games tried from it did not run.
- **It needs a lot of memory:** it is made for devices with a large address space and a memory limit of 6 GB or more, such as an 8 GB iPhone signed with the larger memory limit, or an M-series iPad. An update from Valve can break it.
- **Games and DLC are shared both ways** (**Share games with BCD Dock**, on by default; it takes effect at the next start):
  - **BCD Dock's games show as installed in Steam for Windows,** from the same files: one copy of each game, used by both. Steam may update or check them there. BCD keeps a one-time safety copy of BCD Dock's library records. This part was seen working on one iPhone.
  - **A game you install in Steam for Windows shows in BCD's library** and starts through BCD Dock. BCD neither updates it nor changes its DLC.
  - **Steam keeps BCD Dock's DLC choices.** Valve's client installs every DLC your account owns by itself, such as X-Plane 12's free scenery packs, while BCD installs only the DLC you chose. Before each session BCD tells Steam to leave off the DLC you did not choose. If BCD cannot look a game's DLC up (offline, or not signed in), Steam may still download them. At the end of the session, what you ticked, installed, unticked or removed in Steam goes into BCD's DLC choice.
  - **Not yet tried on a device:** the DLC choices and the other direction of the sharing.
- After a Steam for Windows session, restart BCD before you start a game through BCD Dock.

## New in Settings

None of these has been tried on a device yet.

- **Settings › Recommended settings (new page):** every game BCD has recommended settings for, in the list in use. Search by game name, program or Steam App ID, and filter by Steam, Epic, GOG or DRM-free. A game's page shows how it is matched, its switches, every line with whether your build has it, the lines only a device with less than 10 GB of RAM gets, and its notes. It only reads; nothing is changed from there.
- **Settings › Memory & performance › In the background › CPU limit in the background:** 50% (the standard, unchanged), 65%, 80%, 100% or no limit. It sets how much of one core BCD uses while it keeps a game or a download going in the background. At 50% a big download is slow. iOS closes an app that averages above about 80% for a minute, so 100% and no limit can get BCD closed. It applies the next time you leave BCD.
- **Bug reports carry your last game's log by default** (**Settings › Feedback › Attach my last game's log**).
  - The row names the log: the game, the day and the size. Turn it off and BCD keeps that choice.
  - The log is cleaned on the device before it goes: user names, e-mail addresses, IP addresses and account IDs are taken out.
  - An idea or another message still carries a log only when you turn it on.
- **End the game now:** a game that ignores **Close** used to leave you only the way of closing BCD. After 45 seconds the session's top line says so, and the in-game menu offers **End the game now**. Unsaved progress is lost. Not offered on the Windows desktop or while a game is still starting. A new session also no longer counts a process that an earlier session left running.
- **Frame cap: 20 and 25 FPS** (**Settings › Graphics › Frame cap**, now 20, 24, 25, 30, 40 and 60). Frame generation doubles them to 40 and 50. The cap now also holds Vulkan games, which it did not before, and the HUD judges its colour against it.

## Programs built on Qt 6 (experimental)

Qt 6 programs need Windows' ICU libraries (`icuuc.dll` and `icuin.dll`), which Wine does not have. Such a program ended at once with a missing-library error (c0000135): Bloodborne's PC port launcher, Anki, the Albion launcher. BCD now carries ICU 78.3 (Unicode 17.0), trimmed to what Qt needs, and gives it to a program that asks for it. Bloodborne's launcher has the line in its recommended settings. Auto-tune adds it for another Qt 6 program that stops this way; an older build is told to update. ICU's licence is in the app's notices. Not yet tried on a device.

## Fixed in games (from the logs you sent)

Each was made from a log and checked by tests on a Mac. None has been tried on a device yet.

- **Half-Life 2** stopped within seconds of starting, every time. BCD took the game's first write next to a protected page of its own for a write to the protected page. With `env.MADEIRA_GUARD_NEIGHBOUR_PASS = 1`, in its recommended settings, such a write goes through.
- **The Binding of Isaac** crashed on a memory block that BCD placed outside the part of the address space a 32-bit game can reach. A 32-bit game's memory now stays inside its own part, or the request is refused (`env.MADEIRA_WOW_ALLOC_INSIDE = 1`, in its recommended settings).
- **S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Clear Sky and Call of Pripyat** stopped at a shader whose loop BCD's shader compiler cannot write for Shader Model 3. With `env.MADEIRA_HLSL_LOOP_FALLBACK = 40` the loop is written as up to 40 repeated steps. Their recommended settings carry it.
- **DOOM 3: BFG Edition** crashed in BCD's OpenGL when it asked about an empty sync object (`glIsSync(0)`). That now answers as OpenGL defines it, for every game on BCD's OpenGL.
- **METAL GEAR SOLID V** stopped at "Failed to load SteamAPI". It checks the signature of `steam_api64.dll`, and the chain ends in a root certificate BCD's web list lacks (VeriSign Class 3 Public Primary Certification Authority - G5). With `env.MADEIRA_CODESIGN_ROOTS = 1`, in its recommended settings, that one root, pinned by its SHA-256, counts for code signatures. Nothing is added to the root store, so web connections never use it.
- **Buckshot Roulette** needs `--rendering-driver opengl3` to find a graphics driver. BCD cut a program name at its first blank, so the line for "Buckshot Roulette.exe" never matched. Names with a blank now work in `env.MADEIRA_CHILD_ARGS`, and the game's recommended settings pass the argument.
- **A game that froze for good after a click on its window's frame** (title bar and edges of a windowed game) no longer does. The size and move loop of such a window now takes taps and keys. `env.MADEIRA_GAME_INPUT_WAKE = 0` turns it off.
- **EA games started through Steam** (Battlefield 4, Mass Effect: Andromeda, Need for Speed, STAR WARS Jedi: Fallen Order, The Sims 4, Unravel and others) go through EA's launcher, whose background service needs Windows' service manager. BCD Dock now starts Wine's service manager for a game whose install script runs EA's installer. These games, and FIFA 22 and Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2012), also get the Wine libraries the EA app asks for in their recommended settings.
- **A 64-bit game's big program or library that did not fit the room left in BCD's code memory** was copied anyway, the copy was refused, and the game never started (Cyberpunk 2077's XeSS libraries and others). Such a file now runs from its own file instead.
- **Cyberpunk 2077:** its recommended settings now keep its images out of the code memory and handle its 16, 64 and 32 GB address reservations, and also match its launcher program. Auto-tune has a rule for its overlapping reservations.
- **Spider-Man:** Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered and Miles Morales get the swap file from the first start on devices with less than 10 GB of RAM. Spider-Man 2 gets the per-process keyed event setting.
- **More:** Dark Souls: Remastered is told it has 8 GB, so its minimum-memory box does not stop it. NARUTO: Ultimate Ninja STORM and The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion get a DirectInput view of the controller. TEKKEN 7 and Little Nightmares get Wine's Windows Error Reporting library. eFootball PES 2021 gets Wine's DirectX diagnostics library. Detroit: Become Human gets Vulkan on KosmicKrisp. ULTIMATE MARVEL VS. CAPCOM 3 gets BCD's 64-bit Direct3D 9. FINAL FANTASY TACTICS gets new Direct3D 12 settings. Rows now also name a game's program, so a copy outside Steam gets them too (see the list below).

## Resident Evil 4 (2005) and other Direct3D 9 games: copying only what a draw reads (experimental)

A player's log showed Resident Evil 4 (2005) running at 60 FPS for 30 seconds and then at 4 to 6 FPS. The game locks its dynamic vertex buffers about 210 times a frame, 1 to 256 bytes each, and every draw after a lock copied the whole 3.8 MB buffer to the GPU: 788 MB a frame in the log. The GPU was 5 to 8% busy.

- **New, off unless set:** `env.DXMT_D9_VB_RANGE = 1`. A draw that is not indexed then copies only the vertex bytes it reads. Indexed and instanced draws, draws from the game's own memory and any stream whose layout is doubtful keep the whole copy. With the line off, nothing changes.
- **It is on, through their recommended settings (from build 710), for Resident Evil 4 (2005) and for every game whose logs showed the same copy** (10 MB or more a frame): Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines, Alan Wake, Blur, Ultra Street Fighter IV, Mount & Blade: Warband, Team Fortress 2, Garry's Mod, Left 4 Dead 2, Counter-Strike: Source, Half-Life 2, Half-Life 2: Deathmatch, No More Room in Hell, Call of Duty: World at War, Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Grand Theft Auto IV, The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011), Splinter Cell: Double Agent and Burnout Paradise. Games that draw mostly with indexed draws (the Source engine games, for example) may gain little. The log says `[vb-range] madeira-bcd on`.
- **Not yet tried on a device.** If you play one of these games, please send a log.

## From pull requests

Thank you to the people who sent these.

- **Touch-control editor: select several controls at once.** Drag from an empty spot in the editor to select several buttons or sticks, then move them together, or resize them together with a pinch or the Size slider. Guides appear while you move a control near another one's edge or centre, and it snaps into line. (pull request #69)
- **Teardown: the missing half of the scene.** The game draws much of its world with Direct3D 12 indirect draws that carry several arguments per draw, and BCD skipped them. With `indirect-expand = 1` BCD now draws them from the game's own records. It is off by default, because a game that changes those records after recording would draw stale ones. Teardown's recommended settings turn it on. Tried on one device by the pull request's author. (pull request #67)
- **Auto-tune judges two kinds of sessions correctly** (pull request #64):
  - a line BCD writes about the previous run is no longer read as this session's, so a game that closed after a few seconds is no longer scored as if it had played for minutes;
  - Windows' shortcut helper (`winemenubuilder.exe`), which Wine tries to start and BCD does not ship, no longer makes a session that played look like a crash.
- **A rare crash when a thread ends** (pull request #64), behind a setting that is off by default (`env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_SKIP = 1`). It now also clears the places where the system keeps the first objects of a thread's memory pool. BCD's own tests now pass on the build Mac.

## Auto-tune

27 rules are new and 14 changed. Each has a log it was made from.

- **Steam client stops** now point to **Nov 2026** (see above).
- **New fixes it can try:**
  - a game that checks the memory it is told and refuses to start gets 8 GB told;
  - a game started through EA's Steam launcher gets Windows' service manager;
  - a game that stops with "needs Vulkan" gets Vulkan on KosmicKrisp turned on;
  - a game's .NET runtime that reserved 256 GB of address space gets a 16 GB range;
  - a Java game that stopped right after its first garbage collection gets the simple collector or plain code memory (Project Zomboid, Slay the Spire);
  - an OpenGL game that stopped at a `ChoosePixelFormat` error or at SDL3's "OpenGL 3.2 is required" box gets BCD's own OpenGL driver turned on (Old School RuneScape, Underkeep);
  - a program built on Chromium whose 16 GB request found no room gets a smaller block (Slow Roads);
  - a 32-bit game that plays but spends most of its frame time on slow memory writes gets ordinary memory, kept only if it then plays without the slowdown.
- **Answers that say what to do:**
  - a game started as a program file that asks for Steam ("Steam is not running"): start it from your Steam library through BCD Dock;
  - an EA game that starts itself through EA's Origin launcher: start it with Steam instead;
  - a device where iOS gives BCD only 4 GB: too small for the game. Lower its own texture and shadow settings.
- **It can add a DLL to a game's own list of DLLs.** Until now a rule that wanted one more DLL was skipped when the recommended settings already had a list. It now adds its names after the list's, and never drops one.
- **More starts count as failures,** so a fix is offered after them: a BCD Dock game that showed an error box and drew no frame, a game that closed by itself before its first picture, and a start where the JIT pool was refused. A replay of 6,303 earlier logs changes 24 verdicts, each a failure that had been missed.
- **Several rules were narrowed** so they stop matching games they did not help (the Chromium address-space rule matched 325 earlier logs, and only 65 were the real case).

## Recommended settings

The list went from 88 to 96: 43 games are new and 35 changed. Some of the updated games only gained a program name, so a copy outside Steam gets their settings too.

- **New:**
  - EA games started through Steam: Battlefield 4, Mass Effect: Andromeda, Mass Effect Legendary Edition, Need for Speed (2015), Need for Speed Heat, STAR WARS Jedi: Fallen Order, The Sims 4, Unravel.
  - Action and adventure: Detroit: Become Human, Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition, Bright Memory: Infinite, Resident Evil 4, Resident Evil 4 (2005), Shadow of the Tomb Raider, Little Nightmares, Batman: Arkham Asylum GOTY (Epic Games copy), Half-Life 2, Bloodborne (PC port launcher), DragonSword: Awakening.
  - Fighting and sports: ULTIMATE MARVEL VS. CAPCOM 3, NARUTO: Ultimate Ninja STORM, eFootball PES 2021, Ultra Street Fighter IV.
  - With the Direct3D 9 vertex change only: Alan Wake, Blur, Mount & Blade: Warband, Team Fortress 2, Garry's Mod, Left 4 Dead 2, Half-Life 2: Deathmatch, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 (2011), The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011), Splinter Cell: Double Agent.
  - Other: Teardown (from a pull request), VRChat, Don't Starve, Echo Weaver, Cryptid Park, Old School RuneScape, Slow Roads, Underkeep, We Steal From Old People: The Game, Fields of Mistria.
- **Updated:**
  - X-Plane 12 and Red Dead Redemption 2 (not Steam: its Launcher.exe beside RDR2.exe).
  - Big releases: Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered, Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Cyberpunk 2077, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, HITMAN World of Assassination, FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles, METAL GEAR SOLID V: THE PHANTOM PAIN, DARK SOULS III, Dark Souls: Remastered, Rise of the Tomb Raider, TEKKEN 7, Dead Space (2023).
  - EA, Need for Speed and FIFA: Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2012), Need for Speed: Most Wanted (speed.exe), FIFA 22.
  - The Direct3D 9 vertex change also went into Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines, Call of Duty: Black Ops, Grand Theft Auto IV, Counter-Strike: Source, Call of Duty: World at War, Half-Life 2, No More Room in Hell and Burnout Paradise.
  - Others: Unrailed! 2: Back on Track, Batman: Arkham City GOTY, Requiem: Avenging Angel, S.T.A.L.K.E.R. (X-Ray engine games), Saints Row: The Third, Sleeping Dogs: Definitive Edition, Call of Duty: Black Ops, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, Buckshot Roulette, The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, THE KING OF FIGHTERS XIV, Day of the Tentacle Remastered.

## Fixed: Epic games on an external drive

- **Installs on some external drives were refused for space** although the drive had plenty of room. In one log the drive answered 0 free to the question BCD asked, and every Epic install was refused at once. BCD now reads the drive's free space the way its Steam downloads already do. A tester confirmed it.
- **On a drive BCD asks only for the room the game's files still lack.** exFAT has no sparse files, so a file created at its final size already holds its room.
- **A refused install writes the space it needed and the space it found into the log.**

## Known issues

- **X-Plane 12** is slow (about 13 to 18 FPS of its own in flight at the lowest settings, about 35 shown with frame generation) and has been tried on one iPhone only. Its first start compiles shaders for several minutes.
- **Apple frame interpolation** does not work for Vulkan games on MoltenVK yet.
- **Vulkan frame generation:** the frame-rate limit holds the game's own frames; the generated frames come on top of it.

Install help, game reports and ideas: the BCD-Games Discord is open, https://discord.gg/43TmupTVug

versions.localizedDescription:
# Cloudn 1.4.2

这一版新增 SideStore / AltStore 侧载软件源支持，修复 Instagram 网页登录点「完成」卡住的问题，并带来多项稳定性、解析与性能优化。

## 新增与改进

- **SideStore / AltStore 软件源**：新增 [altstore.json](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mengangs/Cloudn/main/altstore.json) 订阅源并在发版时自动更新；在「设置 › 更新 › 添加侧载软件源」中可一键添加到 SideStore / AltStore 或复制源地址。
- **Instagram 网页登录修复**：支持从 `sessionid` 提取用户 ID 并补全 `ds_user_id`，实时合并页面 `document.cookie`，放宽非登录页重定向时的校验误判，并在未检测到登录态或校验失败时弹出明确提示。
- **并发与稳定性优化**：加强下载与解析任务防重入保护、完善各网盘/视频解析器与分享扩展边界处理，提升列表滚动、实时活动与无障碍体验。

## 安装

推荐通过 SideStore / AltStore 订阅本仓库软件源直接接收更新；也可下载下方附件里的 `Cloudn-v1.4.2.ipa` 自行签名后安装（需要 iOS 17 及以上）。

apps.name: DukeX
apps.subtitle: Original Xbox emulation for iOS
apps.localizedDescription: DukeX is an experimental iOS-focused frontend for xemu. It embeds the xemu core in a native Swift shell and presents the Vulkan renderer through MoltenVK and native Metal.

versions.localizedDescription:
# DukeX v1.0.2 - Expanding the Xbox Experience

DukeX v1.0.2 is our biggest step yet toward preserving the full original Xbox
experience, not just the games. This release introduces the first native macOS
build, expands XB.Live integration, and brings richer community features to both
iOS and macOS.

## What's New

- Native macOS release: DukeX is now available as a Mac Catalyst desktop build
  packaged with a nested Xemu fork, pairing desktop Xemu compatibility with the
  DukeX interface.
- XB.Live Rich Presence and playtime tracking: friends can see what you are
  playing while DukeX tracks supported playtime sessions.
- XB.Live messaging: threaded conversations, friend messaging, unread
  indicators, supported game invites, and existing Xbox inbox support now live
  inside DukeX.
- XB.Live social expansion: friend requests, friend management, online presence,
  and deeper community integration are available from the Profile experience.
- Activity Feed: XB.Live news, friend online status, friend achievement unlocks,
  and community updates now appear in a continuously refreshed timeline.
- Controller Landscape Mode: on iOS, compatible controllers can switch DukeX
  into a controller-first browsing and launch experience.
- Expanded AirPlay and external display support: big-screen play is more
  reliable across supported display configurations.

## Improvements

- Improved achievements with Games, Apps, and Cores grouping plus updated
  artwork handling for XB.Live Core, DukeX Core, and special test titles.
- Improved game tile spacing and cover handling across iOS and macOS.
- Improved XB.Live cloud-save sync metadata with console identity v2,
  content-hash dedupe, and server-assisted cross-console restore handling.
- Fixed achievement progress rounding so time-based achievements do not show
  100% before they are actually complete.

## Availability

- iOS: install `DukeX.v1.0.2.ipa` through StikStore, SideStore, or another
  supported sideloading workflow.
- macOS: install `DukeX.macOS.v1.0.2.dmg` by dragging DukeX to Applications.
- Hardware requirements on iOS remain Apple A14 Bionic or Apple M1 hardware or
  newer.
- iOS 16.0 or later is supported, with iOS 16 support remaining experimental.

## Important

DukeX does not include Xbox system files, game images, BIOS files, copyrighted
content, signing certificates, or user games. Users must provide their own
legally obtained files. DukeX is intended for legitimate emulation,
preservation, testing, and personal library use.

versions.localizedDescription:
## Erosion-CN v1.0.6 (Build 31)

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **System Compatibility / 系统兼容性提示**  
> - **Supported / 完整支持**：`iOS / iPadOS 27.0 – 27.2.1` and `27.3 beta 1` (`24C503*`).  
> - **Patched / 已封堵**：Apple patched `worse_query` starting in **`iOS 27.3 beta 2` (`24C5049d+`)**. Do **NOT** update past `27.3 beta 1` if you rely on Erosion-CN.

---

### What's New / 更新内容

1. **General Splash Ad Blocker Whitelist & Manual Manager (`AdWhitelistStore` / `AdWhitelistManagerSheet`) / 去广告应用与路径通用白名单及手动管理面板** *(Thanks to [@appleoner](https://github.com/appleoner) for suggesting [#56](https://github.com/Kianuni/Erosion-CN/issues/56) / 感谢 [@appleoner](https://github.com/appleoner) 在 [#56](https://github.com/Kianuni/Erosion-CN/issues/56) 提出建议)*
   - **Dedicated Whitelist Manager (`白名单`)**：Added top-bar & Overview card entry points supporting **manual `Bundle ID` / `AppGroup ID` entry**, **quick-picking from installed third-party containers**, **manual container subpath entry**, and one-tap deletion of rules.
   - **Per-App, Per-Path & File Browser Controls**：Whitelist an entire app + its matching `group.<bundleID>` AppGroups from the container `⋯` menu, exempt a specific folder/config via the row **Ignore (`加白`)** button, or long-press any file/folder in **File Browser** → **Add to Ad Whitelist**.
   - **Auto-Skip & Auto-Restore**：Whitelisted apps and paths automatically skip global **Lock All** (`一键全锁`) and immediately restore `0755`/`0644` writable permissions (cleaning `.erosion_adlock`) when added. Includes a removable default crash-guard entry for **SMZDM (`什么值得买` · `com.smzdm.client.ios`)**.

apps.name: Fathom
apps.subtitle: x86-64 PC emulator for iOS
apps.localizedDescription:
An x86-64 PC emulator for iOS. Fathom runs x86-64 Linux programs on an iPhone or iPad by translating them to ARM64 as they execute, using FEXCore - the dynamic recompiler behind FEX-Emu - with a native SwiftUI front end.

Import a statically linked x86-64 Linux executable, open it, press Run. Fathom maps it into a guest address space, hands its instructions to FEXCore's JIT, answers its Linux syscalls, and shows you its output.

JIT requires StikDebug to attach to the process and service the executable-memory traps; Fathom asks for this automatically on launch when it is missing.

Please note: only statically linked, position-independent executables (-static-pie) run today. Dynamically linked binaries and 32-bit x86 are not supported yet, and threads are not implemented, so a guest runs single-threaded.

versions.localizedDescription:
An x86-64 PC emulator for iOS, running guest code on FEXCore.

2048 and tic tac toe both run. Add them from the Library tab and play with the on-screen arrow keys.

**Downloads**
- `Fathom.ipa` - the app, unsigned, for sideloading. Needs StikDebug attached for JIT.
- `tictactoe` - arrows move, Enter places, against a minimax bot that cannot be beaten.
- `play2048` - arrows slide the board.

Copy the two game binaries into Fathom's Programs folder, or import them from the Library tab.

apps.name: Husk
apps.subtitle: Android app launcher for iOS
apps.localizedDescription: Run Android apps on iOS: drop in an APK, tap it, and the Android app opens full-screen on a QEMU guest with hardware-accelerated display and audio. Needs JIT plus a debugger attached at runtime, so it requires a sideloading setup that can provide get-task-allow rather than a plain re-sign.

versions.localizedDescription:
## What's new?

3.4 is a compatibility release. About 97% of the 472 F-Droid apps we test now run, up from 85%. On the 169 Play Store apps we test, about 90% run, not counting apps with anti-tamper or fraud protection, which Husk doesn't try to bypass. All of these numbers are from testing on a Mac.

### More Android apps
- Microsoft Word opens (Excel and PowerPoint share its libraries)
- Slack, Gmail, Teams, Deezer, Flipboard and Picsart get past the crashes that stopped them
- More engines and frameworks start: React Native's new architecture, Qt 6 / QML, and apps using JavaScriptCore
- libGDX and other OpenGL apps draw again (3.3 broke these)
- Apps that keep secrets in Android's secure key store work better
- Apps with big bundled databases open
- UPnP and network discovery apps can start
- Apps that declare their launch screen in a split APK can start

### Looks better
- Rounded buttons are proper pills instead of ellipses
- Toolbars, window backgrounds and more color formats behave like they do on a phone

### Less "out of memory"
- Fewer `OutOfMemoryError: pthread_create` crashes on installs without extended address space
- Unity games use less address space on sideloaded installs, and keep their frame rate up
- New in Settings -> Performance: see whether Increased Memory Limit and Extended Address Space are on for your install

### Also
- Japanese, thanks to @Yuki-1018
- Fixed Husk crashing when importing a `.p12`, or at launch with one saved on iOS 27 (#220)
- The Remove and Uninstall dialogs open next to their buttons on iPad (#218)
- Winlator's Settings page no longer crashes
- Husk builds with Xcode 27 and the iOS 27 SDK

## Known Issues
- Without JIT, Minecraft, some Flutter apps and some LÖVE games can fail. Use StikJIT for those for now
- Browsers (Firefox, Brave, Opera) don't run yet because they need separate helper processes
- Husk's Java runtime still has no garbage collector, so big apps can run out of memory in long sessions (#191)
- Touch doesn't work yet in Godot 3 games (#200)
- Apps with anti-tamper still won't run, and neither will apps that need Google Play services or a Google account
- Winlator containers don't run
- Full Android is still slow. Use the translation layer for games

## Thanks
Thanks to @BartolomeoRusso9, @Dey410 and @Yuki-1018 for their pull requests, and to everyone who sent logs. Crash reports are what made this release possible ❤️

## Links
- Website: https://itslevii.dev

iBuilder turns a Switch game dump you own into a native iOS build on the iPhone itself: extract, rewrite, translate the shaders, sign and play. Experimental: results differ per game.

No game, firmware or key is included or downloaded. Use it only with your own games and the prod.keys of your own console. Not affiliated with Nintendo or Apple.

versions.localizedDescription:
> [!WARNING]
> No game, firmware or key is included or downloaded. Use iBuilder only with games you own and the `prod.keys` dumped from your own console. Not affiliated with Nintendo or Apple.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Every game rebuilds its shaders once** after this update: the shader chain moves to `6c53446391cc` (nxnative 033793f0), and a library is named by its chain. iOS's Metal shader cache also starts empty once, so the first play of each game stutters more.

**New**
- **Shader chain 6c53446391cc**, nxnative's current one: 37 upstream translator and host changes, including the Switch 2 mesh/task fixes. The Rust build gives the same library bytes as upstream (5,348 Ocarina shaders compared).
- **More games found compatible**: shader readers for EA (FIFA 18: 0 → 330 shaders), CRI CPK, Diablo III, Unreal IoStore and encrypted paks, Smash Bros. Ultimate, Trinity (stored files), Frostbite (stored data), TT Games DAT, Larian LSPK, Blizzard CASC, Camelot CRA, PDAT, Rockstar RPF6, REDengine, RAGE WAD, NXCX, Telltale, GIANTS SHARC, Virtuos VBF, UbiArt IPK v5, MT Framework ARC v9. OpenGL and Vulkan games get their shaders too (glslang is now in the app; the engine compiles them on the phone).
- **Build screen: Mode Cool / Fast** in place of Close. Cool (default) keeps the app smooth and the phone cooler; Fast builds at full speed, hotter. A running build follows a change.
- **Faster builds**: a per-shader stream instead of batches; a rebuild after an update or a DLC reuses the shaders that did not change; a build resumed after iOS ended the app keeps half its threads instead of one. The build log now shows where the time went (translator, SPIRV-Cross, cores busy, translator GC).
- **Settings**: *Check the shader cache* (on: a game iOS's cache forgot after a reboot or an iOS update is prepared again), *Faster shader preparation* (off: the device's full compiler concurrency when cool or charging), *Optimized translator (experimental)* (off: smaller shaders, may show graphics errors).
- Shader libraries compiled for size (`optimizationLevel = Size`, the engine and the preparation alike).

**Known limits**
- Still refused: Oodle-compressed shaders (Octopath Traveler 0, FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, Yoshi and the Mysterious Book, Mario & Luigi: Brothership, EA SPORTS FC 27, LEGO Star Wars base game, Pokémon Legends: Z-A), XNB LZX, Next Level Games archives; Camelot games need a capture of their file-table NRO.
- The new readers are checked against nxnative on synthetic games, not on every real game; FIFA 18 is split and translated, not yet played. Nothing in this release has been played on an iPhone before publishing.

**Install**: SideStore source `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Absenti/iBuilder/main/apps.json`, or the `.ipa` below. Bundle id `dev.ibuilder.app`, iOS 26+, iPhone 12 or later. Assets: the `.ipa`, its `.sha256`, and `.ipa.verify.tar.gz` (the verifier that checked it: 261 checks passed).

apps.subtitle: Steam Big Picture on iPhone and iPad
apps.localizedDescription: Run Valve’s Steam client in Big Picture and compatible Windows PC games locally on iPhone and iPad through Madeira, Wine, FEX and Metal. Experimental; requires iOS 26+, JIT, and user-provided Steam files.

versions.localizedDescription:
# Steam64 setup, one step at a time

**Experimental prerelease · Build145 · Known issue: Steam can freeze after the third game exit. This update improves setup; it does not fix that stability issue.**

## What’s new

- **Install Steam64 in the launcher:** downloads the matched Steam/browser packages from Valve over HTTPS, verifies sizes/SHA-256 and installs with rollback. Cancel/retry, Verify/Repair and Return to previous environment are available.
- **Four clear actions:** Install Steam → Connect LocalDevVPN → Pair this device → Enable JIT. Runtime preparation is automatic, signing/address checks remain mandatory, completed steps are checked/skipped and the view follows the next action.
- **Pair in iDeck:** starts the existing on-device pairing immediately with live instructions/PIN, without hunting through JIT settings. iOS calls the pairing host Madeira. Advanced methods/import/recovery/account/auto-start settings are collapsed.
- **Data stays yours:** the original environment remains intact; no auth cache, game or save is silently transferred. Use Valve’s own login and Steam Guard yourself.

## Install and test

Download `iDeck-0.1.3-alpha.6-build145.ipa` and `SHA256SUMS`, verify the hash, then sign/sideload using your own coherent development main/helper profiles. Keep `MadeiraJITHelper.appex` and debugging permission; signing alone does not activate JIT. Back up saves and keep the same app identity when upgrading—uninstalling can erase local data.

Open iDeck and follow the highlighted setup step; fully close/reopen when prompted after installing Steam64. For on-device pairing use iOS27; iOS26 offers pairing-file import. Activate JIT again for each new app process.

The IPA includes the local runtime and pinned source-built open support components, **no Valve Steam client/libcef, games, accounts, maintainer profile or pairing file**. The installer acquires the client from Valve. Both source companions, relink, license/audit and inventory/checksum assets accompany this release.

## What was verified

The user reports Build144 installation can complete. Build145 passed host ordering/skip/restart/signing/VA checks, installer/rollback/privacy regressions, existing JIT integration checks and full Xcode compilation. Its separate Fresh Test version was development-signed, installed/read back and opened on an iPhone15ProMax; original iDeck was preserved. The public ad-hoc IPA was audited (1480files, no findings), and its105-input relink ran with all30TEXT section hashes matching.

The complete revised145 first-run UI, another-device sideload/JIT, new Steam login and repeated gameplay have **not** received a new acceptance result; the public IPA was not installed again after ad-hoc packaging. iPad, Bluetooth and arbitrary games are not validated by this release. Full independent-machine/offline runtime rebuilding is not claimed.

## Limits that still matter

- **Third game return may freeze Steam.** Report the first failing stage and game-cycle count.
- Steam64 does **not** enlarge the device’s virtual address space. Unsupported layouts can still fail;32-bit games/helpers may still hit separate limits. Guards remain enabled.
- The compatibility snapshot is **Steam manifest1769025840 (January22,2026), CEF126**, held to its matched components. It is not the latest Steam/Chromium and has security/compatibility limitations; future snapshots need fresh review.
- Game support remains limited. No DRM, authentication or anti-cheat bypass is provided. Never post credentials, Steam Guard data, pairing files, profiles or raw personal logs.

See [the four-step guide](https://github.com/kuscholar/iDeck/blob/v0.1.3-alpha.6/docs/STEAM64_SETUP.md), [Build145 evidence](https://github.com/kuscholar/iDeck/blob/v0.1.3-alpha.6/docs/release/BUILD145_RESULTS.md) and the bilingual README.

## iPadn 2.3.5

**目录 / Contents**：[简体中文](#-核心修复与优化) · [TestFlight 说明与免责](#-testflight-实验性说明与免责声明) · [English](#english) · [TestFlight Notice](#testflight-experimental-notice--disclaimer)

本次为 **v2.3.5** 稳定性修复与体验升级版：根治 **iOS 16.0–16.2 强链接符号闪退**、**iOS 27.2 beta 2 历史版本加载闪退** 与 **iPadOS 全屏/专业模式导航栏异常**；**TestFlight 现支持切换下载 Apple TV 等多平台测试包**并统一展示单色客户端标识，同时修复大型/多变体游戏误报「产物校验失败，已清理」及详情页顶部虚化异常；在「设置 › 外观与图标」开放**自定义全部 177 个 Apple 商店地区**（支持搜索筛选、勾选、拖拽排序与国旗展示）；并修复 FairPlay 高熵插件误拒、登录 `5020`/2FA 提示、未购免费应用首次获取旧版报错与「应用包」批量导入打断问题。安装包均未签名，请使用自用签名工具签名后安装。

### 🔧 核心修复与优化

- **修复 iOS 16/27 闪退与 iPadOS 专业模式导航异常**
  - 移除强链接 iOS 17+/18+ 的 `UnevenRoundedRectangle` 与全部 `.onGeometryChange` 调用，改用向后兼容路径与几何读取实现，根治 iOS 16.0 / 16.0.2 / 16.2 打开界面或卡片时因动态符号缺失导致的闪退。
  - 修复 iOS 27.2 beta 2 在应用详情页加载历史版本时偶发崩溃的问题（修正版本行布局优先级与骨架屏几何回调防抖阈值）。
  - 修复 iPadOS 全屏及开启「专业模式」后导航栏切换错乱、标题丢失与工具栏按钮跨标签泄露的问题，改为按当前活动标签隔离独立导航栈。
- **TestFlight 支持 Apple TV 多平台下载、校验修复与顶部优化**
  - TestFlight 详情页新增多平台切换（如 `iOS` / `Apple TV`），支持直接下载 Apple TV（tvOS）测试包，并与同一应用的 iOS 测试包独立索引、互不覆盖。
  - 在「下载」「应用包」「存储空间」「包体详情」「解密详情」等全应用页面为 Apple TV 等非 iPhone 包并列展示单色客户端图标（紧邻单色 TestFlight 图标）；点击 TestFlight 任务与安装包详情均可查看来源、客户端与对应最低系统版本（如 `tvOS`）；Apple TV 测试包下载后与常规商店包一致不显示「安装」按钮且不触发自动安装。
  - 修复 TestFlight 下载大型/多变体游戏（如多架构或超大二进制包）误报「产物校验失败，已清理」的问题：改用流式读取 Mach-O 头部前缀并兼容 FAT 32/64 位架构 `cryptid` 校验，修正替换 SINF 计数与完整变体（`packages.full`）筛选逻辑。
  - 修复进入 TestFlight 应用详情页时顶部状态栏与封面衔接处出现浅色虚化断层的显示异常，改用不透明模糊与导航栏原生外观平滑衔接。
- **设置开放自定义 177 个商店地区（支持搜索筛选与排序）**
  - 在「设置 › 外观与图标 › 商店地区」开放自定义管理搜索页显示的地区列表，覆盖全部 **177** 个 Apple App Store 商店地区（补齐 `AF`、`LI`）。
  - 支持按中文名称、英文名称或 ISO‑2 地区代码实时搜索筛选（精确匹配代码优先置顶）、点击勾选、拖拽排序、国旗与代码同屏展示及一键「恢复默认」（至少保留 1 个地区）。
- **修复 FairPlay 解密误拒、首次获取旧版报错与批量导入体验**

**v2.3.5** delivers key stability fixes and highly requested improvements: eliminates **iOS 16.0–16.2 strong-linked symbol crashes**, **iOS 27.2 beta 2 version-history crashes**, and **iPadOS full-screen / Pro mode toolbar & navigation bugs**; adds **multi-platform TestFlight downloads (including Apple TV)** with monochrome client badges, fixes false validation rejections on large/multi-variant games, and polishes the TestFlight detail top blur; opens a searchable, reorderable **177-region Storefront picker** under Settings › Appearance & icon; and resolves FairPlay high-entropy false rejections, login `5020`/2FA messaging, first-time free-app license retries, and multi-IPA batch import interruptions. #### Fixes & Improvements Since v2.3.4

- **Fix iOS 16/27 Crashes & iPadOS Pro Mode Navigation**
  - Removes strong-linked iOS 17+/18+ `UnevenRoundedRectangle` and all `.onGeometryChange` usages in favor of backward-compatible paths and geometry observers, resolving launch and view crashes on iOS 16.0 / 16.0.2 / 16.2.

  - Improves App Store sign-in `5020` / 2FA messaging and adds staged `SAPSigner` failure diagnostics.
  - Automatically invalidates stale version caches and performs short backoff retries after acquiring a free app license so first-time older-version fetches no longer fail on transient `9610` delays.
  - Fixes multi-IPA batch import in **Packages** prematurely opening a detail sheet mid-batch, adding live `(done/total)` progress, batch completion toast, and a dismissible error banner.

versions.localizedDescription:
# Iridium 0.2.0

Download your Steam games directly in Iridium, manage repairs and updates, and try the updated Windows runtime. Game support remains experimental.

## Download

**[Download Iridium (.ipa)](https://github.com/intraducine/iridium/releases/download/v0.2.0/Iridium-unsigned.ipa)**

Requires **iOS or iPadOS 18+**, JIT, and games you own. You only need the IPA to install; supply your own game files or download owned games from Steam.

## Install

1. Sign and install the IPA and helper with a compatible sideloading tool, or import it into LiveContainer using its supported JIT setup.
2. Open Iridium and configure JIT in **Launch Support**.
3. Open **Downloads → Steam** to sign in and queue a game, or use **Add Game** to import a game folder. Choose its executable, add it to your library, then press **Play**.

For standalone installation, preserve `com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit=true` in both Iridium's final app signature and provisioning profile. The anonymous ad-hoc carrier alone grants no installation or memory rights. In LiveContainer, the container process's signature, profile, and JIT setup determine effective rights; importing the guest IPA does not grant them. Both routes still need device validation.

Back up your saves before updating. Update the existing app or LiveContainer entry without deleting its data. Steam repairs and updates keep older installations; saves stored inside an older game folder may need to be copied manually to the new one. Keep that older folder until you have checked your saves.

## What's new

- **Steam downloads in the app.** Sign in with a password or QR code, with Steam Guard support, browse your library, and choose download language, unprotected branch, 32/64-bit files, and owned DLC.
- **A download queue with verification and repair.** Pause, resume, retry, and prioritize downloads. Check for updates or repair downloaded files while keeping the previous installation.
- **Clearer storage warnings.** Download checks use the space available to Iridium and account for verified partial files. **Download Anyway** can bypass an estimated-space warning for one attempt; file verification and real out-of-space errors remain enforced.
- **Updated Windows runtime.** Includes 32-bit WoW64 support and D3D9/D3D12 updates. Support still varies by game and device.
- **Game prerequisite installers.** Run supported setup steps included with a game, or choose **Game Options → Run Installer** for an EXE or MSI installer you provide. Some installers need interaction. Closing the player requests cancellation; Iridium keeps observing the runtime's exit and reports when a restart is required.
- **Reduced duplicate runtime data.** Identical Windows runtime files share one packaged copy. The main app's anonymous ad-hoc signature carries only the increased-memory-limit request; helpers remain unsigned until you sign them.

## Known issues

- Physical-device compatibility for these changes has not been established. Some games may fail to launch or have graphics, video, audio, input, save, or shutdown problems. Skyrim speech and mouse attack issues remain unverified.
- Keep Iridium open while downloading. Downloads pause when the app goes into the background and need to be resumed. Real-account downloads and recovery after Wi-Fi or network loss still need device testing.
- Steam Cloud, Workshop, Steam Families library discovery, password-protected branches, and desktop Steam services are not included. Games that require Steamworks/DRM, anti-cheat, or other unsupported runtime features may not launch after downloading.
- Updates keep older game copies and need extra storage. **Download Anyway** does not create free space; exhausting device storage can also prevent other apps from saving.
- JIT and available memory depend on your device and signing setup; LiveContainer and standalone results can differ. Built-in JIT requires standalone Iridium, debugging permission, a valid pairing file, and LocalDevVPN. Hosted Iridium uses external JIT. Recipient signing, LiveContainer hosting, and game prerequisite success still need device testing.

<details>
<summary>Source code, licenses, and build details</summary>

## Source and licenses

The other release files are for source access, rebuilding, and download verification:

- Download both `Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part01` and `.part02` for the complete matching source package.
- `Iridium-source-guide.zip` contains license notices, source records, and build/relink instructions.
- `SHA256SUMS` verifies the IPA, both source parts, and the source guide.

Download all five release files into one folder, then run:

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
cat Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part01 Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz.part02 > Iridium-corresponding-source.tar.gz
unzip Iridium-source-guide.zip
shasum -a 256 -c Iridium-source-guide/ASSEMBLED-SHA256SUMS
```

The source guide includes the assembled archive's checksum and rebuild instructions. Keep the matching source and guide beside the IPA at this versioned release URL. GitHub's automatic repository ZIP does not contain all required dependency sources.

Source commit: b7e24f9fb4dd17f5d940c4763123f2b00d0e121f
Build run: https://github.com/intraducine/iridium/actions/runs/37142663989

App and helper version: **0.2.0 (115.1)**, minimum iOS **18.0**, confirmed in the actual delivered Info.plist files. The IPA is **399,916,792 bytes**; SHA-256 `1934922a1fcf1509e305a29d6f0d26579a4318ba95dfcf5b406d5e38f88c9763`.

Source checks, Steam native/simulator checks, the full app build, and final binary/package checks passed. Independent IPA inspection confirmed the exact anonymous XML/DER entitlement carrier with no CMS payload or team identity, eight unsigned non-main native binaries, strict bundle verification, runtime hashes, and ZIP modes and symlinks. Unchanged runtime component outputs were reused after provenance checks. These checks do not establish real-account login, owned-game downloads, game compatibility, recipient signing, or physical-device behavior.

Apple compiler-runtime notice uncertainty and unsigned-IPA contractual authorization remain documented risks. Retain the license guide in `Iridium-source-guide.zip`.

</details>

versions.localizedDescription:
# LinuxRunner v1.0.1

Linux on your iPhone and iPad. This update adds iPad desktop adaptations, brings Arch Linux ARM into the setup workflow and improves package recovery and desktop sessions.

## What's New

- **iPad support:** window-aware desktop sizing, hardware-keyboard desktop shortcuts and the shared touch/pointer interface. Tested on a physical iPad.
- **Arch Linux ARM:** install signed packages, use `pacman` and explore an experimental Openbox desktop with LXQt Panel and PCManFM-Qt.
- **One setup workflow:** **Distributions → Set Up Linux…** installs a distribution or configures an existing environment while preserving its files and accounts.

The maintainer reports a working Arch graphical desktop and graphical application launches on a physical iPhone using **build 897**. Telegram Desktop has been tested on Arch Linux ARM with login, sending messages and calls. The supplied iPhone capture shows its welcome screen.

## Improvements

Arch desktop defaults provide a visible panel, wallpaper and file manager without replacing the user's normal LXQt configuration. Managed graphical launches share the active account's authenticated X11 context. Desktop startup status and Qt diagnostics are more useful when a component fails.

IPA packaging now includes an ad-hoc code signature and a standard ZIP layout. It still needs a compatible signing/provisioning method for ordinary device installation.

## Bug Fixes

- Arch terminal termios2 compatibility.
- Signed cached-package recovery and consistent handling of orphaned GCC ownership/obsolete recovery state.
- Qt X11 launch-context failures and desktop profile defaults.
- Reopening existing desktop sessions and readiness after component crashes.
- ARM64 vDSO executable mapping and covered filesystem/syscall compatibility gaps.

## Supported Distributions

| Distribution | Experience |
| --- | --- |
| Debian GNU/Linux 13 ARM64 | Recommended terminal and LinuxRunner Desktop; KDE Plasma remains experimental. |
| Arch Linux ARM | Terminal, `pacman` and experimental Openbox/LXQt-component desktop. |
| Alpine Linux 3.24 ARM64 | Small terminal environment with `apk`; graphical compatibility remains experimental. |

## Installation

Download the release IPA and sign/install it with your preferred compatible sideloading tool, such as Sideloadly or AltStore Classic. Then use **Distributions → Set Up Linux…** to install Linux inside the app.

See the [installation guide](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner#installation) and [Linux setup walkthrough](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner/blob/v1.0.1/docs/GETTING_STARTED.md). When updating, back up important files and preserve the existing app identity and App Group configuration. Do not uninstall the app as a repair step.

## Known Limitations

The application interprets ARM64 Linux userspace; it does not boot a Linux kernel, require JIT or use hardware virtualization. System-call and application coverage is incomplete. The configured minimum is iOS/iPadOS 15.0; model/OS compatibility is not universal. iPad support has been physically tested. An older iPhone 11/iOS 17 launch-black-screen report is unresolved.

Arch desktop, Debian KDE Plasma and Metal acceleration remain experimental. Arch Plasma/Wayland is unavailable. Some Arch GTK/glycin programs still encounter write-seal compatibility problems. Large applications can be slow or exceed memory limits. iOS/iPadOS may suspend or terminate the app; saved files persist, running processes do not survive termination.

## Downloads

- **LinuxRunner-1.0.1.ipa** — ad-hoc signed, without an Apple provisioning profile. Install with your preferred compatible signing/sideloading method.
- **LinuxRunner-1.0.1-source.tar.gz** — matching application source and build scripts, pinned build dependencies, matching Alpine source inputs and terminal-renderer sources.
- **LICENSES.txt** — project and third-party license notices.
- **SHA256SUMS** — checksums for the IPA, source archive and license notices.

The IPA is **14,646,386 bytes**. Verify the original download before signing it; signing changes its checksum.

```text
c571c7ae1dd8ab641930e513254866658dc94f0bee370f1d2623cd462f0fa2ca  LinuxRunner-1.0.1.ipa
```

GitHub automatic source archives omit submodule contents. Use the separately attached source asset for the dependency-inclusive source distribution.

## Feedback and License

[Report reproducible problems through GitHub Issues](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner/issues/new/choose), including your device, OS, app version/build, distribution and diagnostic report. Review logs/screenshots for personal information before attaching them.

LinuxRunner derives from [iSH](https://github.com/ish-app/ish) through [ios-linuxkit](https://github.com/rcarmo/ios-linuxkit). The combined application is GPL-3.0-covered; upstream copyright, contribution-specific terms, App Store terms and third-party notices are preserved. See the repository's [license](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner/blob/v1.0.1/LICENSE.md) and [third-party notices](https://github.com/mxhm11cr/LinuxRunner/blob/v1.0.1/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

apps.name: LiveContainer+SideStore
apps.subtitle: Run iOS apps without actually installing them!
apps.localizedDescription: An app launcher that runs iOS apps without actually installing them. This build of LiveContainer comes with a built-in SideStore for refreshing your apps.

versions.localizedDescription:
**Commit:** [b0f53e8934df325970e9b6ff52932a43b585c424](https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/commit/b0f53e8934df325970e9b6ff52932a43b585c424)
**Message:** fix build

This is a nightly release [created automatically with GitHub Actions workflow](https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/actions/runs/44759628484/attempts/1).

# ⚠️This build is OUTDATED. Please use [nightly version](https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/releases/tag/nightly) instead.

# LiveContainer 3.8.0

> [!Warning]
> The standalone version requires **SideStore 0.6.2+** or **AltStore 2.2.1+** for installation.
> To install LiveContainer with built-in SideStore (`LiveContainer+SideStore.ipa`), please use [Impactor](https://github.com/khcrysalis/Impactor) or [iloader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader). See [our installation guide](https://livecontainer.github.io/docs/installation/lc_sidestore) for details.

# New Features

## Storage Management

- Added a new storage management view with a breakdown of app bundles, containers, temporary files, app group data, tweaks, and other files. (Hidden apps' size is included in "other" section until unlocked)
- Added per-app storage details, including app bundle size, container sizes, and last-used date.
- Added actions to clean temporary files and caches, including guest app caches and LiveContainer's own caches.

## Multiple LiveContainers
- Added configurable launch priority for multiple LiveContainer instances, making shared-app shortcuts choose available instances in the order you prefer. (#1367)

## Share to Apps in LiveContainer
Added a share extension to LiveContainer. When you share a URL or a file from iOS's share sheet, LiveContainer will ask which app you would like to open the URL/file in, so the old share to LiveContainer shortcut method is no longer needed. When an ipa file is shared in this way, LiveContainer will ask if you want to install it in LiveContainer or in the built-in SideStore (if installed) (#1357)

## Multitasking

- Added per-app multitask preferences. Each app can now follow the global setting, always launch in multitask mode, or avoid multitask mode. (#1208)
- Improved multitask dock behavior: the dock can be made smaller, hidden more cleanly, and has improved padding. (#1228, #1250)
- Added more multitask window animations and improved native-window scene handling.
- URL schemes and `open-url` payloads can be passed to already-running multitask apps and native windows.

## JIT
- Added StosDebug support as a JIT enabler.

## TweakLoader
You can now disable tweaks in the "Tweaks" page in LiveContainer's UI. by @SAOMDVN

# Improvements
- Added support for manually setting a container's IDFV. (#1194)
- IDFV spoofing works even when Tweakloader is not loaded.
- Reworked signing logic for tweaks and app installation, with multithreaded signing support.
- Download alerts now block tab switching while a download is in progress.
- Crash reports are shown in a sheet instead of a large alert for better performance on newer iOS versions.
- Add a "Clear Notification" button (#1388)
- Added some popular NSBonjourServices keys so apps can discover AirPlay devices and remote pairing pairable hosts in the local network. (#1417)

# Bug Fixes

- Fixed `livecontainer://open-url` dropping the deep link when launching an app from a cold start. (#1339)
- Fixed the Add to Home Screen menu failing or behaving incorrectly by replacing the SwiftUI context menu implementation. (#1209)
- Fixed a crash when opening Container Preferences if the app did not contain an `en.lproj` path. (#1239)
- Fixed apps and AltStore sources not being searchable in some cases. (#1365, #1368)
- Fixed converting a shared app back to private after aborting an install with the same bundle identifier, which could leave stale container state behind. (#1347)
- Fixed shortcuts and JIT flows getting stuck on a busy LiveContainer instance instead of using another available instance. (#1386)
- Fixed file picker not workings for some apps because Tweakloader is not loaded after enabling "Hide LiveContainer from dyld API". (#1430)
- Fixed several app launch compatibility issues on iOS 26.5 beta, and some multitask/JIT app launches. (#1300, #1310, #1329)
- Fixed multitask keyboard focus issues on iOS 17.4+, including cases where the keyboard would not appear, Passwords would immediately close, or video playback would freeze in multitask mode. (#1402, #844, #870)
- Added support for iOS 27 developer beta. (#1394, #1417, #1416)
- Fix background downloads in multitask apps (choosing "Keep App Extensions (Register App ID for Each Extension)" is required). (#1415)

# Localization

- Updated translations. Added Spanish translation by @Deci8BelioS

# Credits

Thanks to everyone who contributed code, fixes, testing, and reports for this release, including @boa-z, @ruri1208, @Project516, @yazdipour, @stossy11, and @SAOMDVN.

Great thanks to everyone who helped translate LiveContainer.
